ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Power of Friendliness / How to Make Effective Slides

fullPassage:
It's good to see you, everyone! I'm Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It's fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need. Now, this raises some interesting questions: where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important? To answer these questions, I'd like to tell you about my childhood companion dog, Sparky. When we played with a ball, I noticed that he responded well to my gestures.
The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
I'll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
Now let's turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
A successful presentation relies on employing various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures, making natural eye contact, and speaking with an appropriate volume. But just as important, well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively conveying your message. Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to focus more on listening than on reading. Next, prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally achieved with a font size of at least 18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides with high-quality images that complement the text. By following these simple tips, you can create effective slides that hold your audience's interest and keep them engaged from start to finish!

questions.passage: He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures ①<u>compared</u> to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food ②<u>hidden</u> under only one of them. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, ③<u>paying</u> no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform ④<u>good</u> than the wolves.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④good→better: than이 있으므로 비교급 better가 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ good → better: 'perform better than'에서 비교급 필요
❌ ① compared: compared to ~ 분사구문 올바름
❌ ② hidden: with + O + p.p. 수동 올바름
❌ ③ paying: 분사구문(동시 동작) 올바름
det.tip: 비교급: good → better, well → better. than이 있으면 반드시 비교급

questions.passage: They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't ①<u>becoming</u> wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably ②<u>provided</u> them with a survival advantage that ③<u>allowed</u> their population to grow ④<u>larger</u> than that of wolves.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①becoming→became: 등위접속사 and로 연결된 병렬구조에서 evolved와 같은 과거시제 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① becoming → became: those that didn't became — 앞의 evolved와 병렬
❌ ② provided: 과거시제 올바름
❌ ③ allowed: 관계대명사절 동사 올바름
❌ ④ larger: 비교급 올바름
det.tip: 병렬구조: A evolved into dogs, and B became wolves. 등위접속사 and 양쪽은 같은 형태

questions.passage: When placed with partners ①<u>that</u> the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when ②<u>paired</u> with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos solved the problem regardless of ③<u>that</u> individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a ④<u>cooperative</u> and friendly nature.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③that→which: 'regardless of which individual'에서 의문형용사 which가 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ that → which: regardless of which individual = 어떤 개체든 상관없이. 의문형용사 which가 명사 individual 앞에 필요
❌ ① that: 관계대명사 목적격(partners that the chimpanzees knew) 올바름
❌ ② paired: 분사구문(when paired) 올바름
❌ ④ cooperative: 형용사 올바름
det.tip: which vs that: 'regardless of which ~' = 어떤 ~이든 상관없이. 전치사 of 뒤에는 which(의문사)

questions.passage: Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be ①<u>intelligent</u> and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles. Despite these ②<u>attributes</u>, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted ③<u>cooperation</u>, while Neanderthals tended to live in ④<u>larger</u> groups.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④larger(더 큰)→smaller(더 작은): 네안데르탈인은 더 '작은' 집단에서 살았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ larger(더 큰)가 부적절 → 원문은 smaller(더 작은). 호모 사피엔스가 larger communities, 네안데르탈인이 smaller groups
❌ ① intelligent: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② attributes: 원문 그대로 적절 — 특성/속성
❌ ③ cooperation: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: smaller(더 작은) ↔ larger(더 큰). 문맥 단서: while(대조) — Homo sapiens larger ↔ Neanderthals smaller

questions.passage: First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to focus more on listening than on reading. Next, prioritize ①<u>readability</u> by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. Lastly, ②<u>diminish</u> your slides with high-quality images that complement the text. By following these simple tips, you can create ③<u>effective</u> slides that hold your audience's ④<u>interest</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ②diminish(줄이다/떨어뜨리다)→enhance(향상시키다): 고품질 이미지로 슬라이드를 '향상'시켜야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② diminish(감소시키다)가 부적절 → 원문은 enhance(향상시키다). 고품질 이미지로 보완하는 맥락.
❌ ① readability: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ effective: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ interest: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: enhance(향상시키다) ↔ diminish(감소시키다). 문맥 단서: 'with high-quality images that complement' — 보완/향상

ch: fear of being punished by humans
a sense of friendliness toward humans
questions.passage: Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and __________. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개는 인간과의 의사소통 능력과 인간에 대한 친화감(a sense of friendliness toward humans)을 발달시켰다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ a sense of friendliness toward humans: 원문과 일치, 글의 주제
❌ ① strict training: 본문에 훈련 언급 없음
❌ ② fear of punishment: 맥락과 무관
❌ ③ genetic mutations: 본문에 돌연변이 언급 없음
det.tip: 핵심: dogs ≠ wolves 차이 = communicative skills + friendliness. 글 전체 주제와 연결

ch: cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge
questions.passage: Neanderthals were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted __________. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리 조상은 협력과 지식의 자유로운 교환(cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge)을 촉진하는 공동체에 살았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge: 원문, 사회적 차이의 핵심
❌ ① aggressive behavior: 글의 주제와 반대
❌ ② genetic superiority: 네안데르탈인의 특성
❌ ④ isolation: 반대 — larger communities = 비고립
det.tip: Despite(~에도 불구하고) 뒤 역전: 물리적 열세에도 사회적 협력이 생존의 열쇠

ch: Dr. Wilson의 어린 시절 반려견 이름은 Sparky이다.
한 친절한 학생이 Dr. Wilson을 강연장까지 안내했다.

❌ ④ 불일치: 보노보는 'solved the problem'

ch: 각 슬라이드에는 5줄 이내의 텍스트를 사용해야 한다.

ch: Friendliness as a Key to Survival and Success
Why Neanderthals Were Superior to Homo Sapiens
Competition: The Driving Force of Evolution
questions.passage: Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage. Bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature that has helped their species survive. It was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived through larger communities and cooperation. I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② 친화성이 생존과 성공의 열쇠이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Friendliness as a Key to Survival and Success: 글 전체 주제 — 개, 보노보, 호모사피엔스의 사례
❌ ① 개 가축화 역사: 부분적 소재일 뿐
❌ ③ 네안데르탈인 우월: 글의 결론과 반대
❌ ④ 경쟁이 진화의 원동력: 글의 주제와 정반대
det.tip: 글의 부제가 힌트: 'Soft but Strong' = 부드럽지만 강한 = 친절이 힘

ch: 생존 경쟁에서 협력과 친절이 물리적 힘보다 중요하다는 것

침팬지가 보노보보다 사회적으로 더 발달했다는 것

det.korean: ① 생존 경쟁에서 협력과 친절이 물리적 힘보다 중요하다.

❌ ② 네안데르탈인 지능 비교는 주된 요점이 아님
❌ ③ 침팬지 > 보노보는 원문과 반대
❌ ④ 강한 개체 생존은 화자가 반박하는 기존 관점
det.tip: However + alternative view = 화자의 핵심 주장. kindness > strength

det.korean: ② 각 개인이 조화를 이루며 협력할 때 사회가 더 아름다워진다.

det.analysis: 본문: 'Think of our society as a bouquet' → 패러프레이징: 사회를 bouquet에 비유
det.tip: bouquet = 꽃다발. Think of A as B = A를 B로 생각하다

questions.passage: Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and __________ (physical) superior to Homo sapiens.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 네안데르탈인은 지적이고 신체적으로(physically) 호모 사피엔스보다 우월했다.
det.analysis: 형용사 superior를 수식하므로 부사 physically 필요. physical(형용사) → physically(부사)
det.tip: physical(형용사: 신체적인) → physically(부사: 신체적으로). 부사 + 형용사: physically superior

[ a / survival / advantage / with / probably / the friendly nature / provided / them / of dogs ]

※ 모두 사용하시오. 대소문자 구분 없음.

det.korean: 개의 친화적 본성이 아마도 그들에게 생존 이점을 제공했다.
det.analysis: the friendly nature of dogs(주어) + probably(부사) + provided(동사) + them(간접목적어) + with(전치사) + a survival advantage(직접목적어)
det.tip: provide A with B = A에게 B를 제공하다. probably는 동사 앞에 위치

questions.stem:

det.korean: 협력이 호모 사피엔스에게 경쟁적 이점을 주어 끊임없이 변화하는 환경에 적응(adapt to an ever-changing environment)할 수 있게 했다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment'
det.tip: adapt to = ~에 적응하다. ever-changing = 끊임없이 변화하는
